paragraphs: A church in Dublin has two new coloured glass windows. They help people remember those who died from Aids.
The church is St Teresa's Church on Donore Avenue. It is 100 years old this year. The windows went in before World Aids Day on 1 December.
The windows show people of different ages and cultures. This shows that Aids can affect anyone. A red ribbon and a rainbow are in the pictures.
There is also an alphabet at the bottom. Visitors can spell the name of a person they lost.
People from the church made the design. A church member paid for the windows. The church says they are for everyone.
sentZh: 都柏林一間教堂有了兩扇新的彩色玻璃窗。
它們是為了紀念死於愛滋病的人。
這間教堂是位於多諾爾大道的聖德蕾莎教堂。
今年它剛好一百歲。
這些窗戶在 12 月 1 日世界愛滋病日之前裝好。
窗上畫著不同年齡和文化背景的人。
這表示愛滋病可能影響任何人。
圖中有一條紅絲帶和一道彩虹。
底部還有一排字母。
訪客可以拼出他們失去的人的名字。
教會的人設計了圖案。
一位教友出錢買下這些窗戶。
教會說這些窗戶是為所有人而設的。

paragraphs: A Dublin church has put in two stained-glass windows to remember people who died from Aids. The windows at St Teresa's Church on Donore Avenue were installed before World Aids Day on 1 December, in the year the church turns 100.

The windows show people of different ages and backgrounds. The church says this reminds us that Aids does not choose who it affects. One window has a red Aids ribbon, a message to remember those who died, and the red rose of St Teresa.

A rainbow starts in one window and continues in the other. The second window has a green carnation for the writer Oscar Wilde and the logo of St James's Hospital, to thank doctors and nurses. An alphabet at the bottom lets visitors spell the name of someone they lost.
The windows were designed by parishioners and the parish team, and a parishioner paid for them. A local company, Capital Glass, made and fitted them.
The parish said the windows are for everyone, and people can understand them in their own way. The church already has two windows for people who died during the Covid pandemic.
sentZh: 都柏林一間教堂裝設了兩扇彩繪玻璃窗，紀念死於愛滋病的人。
多諾爾大道聖德蕾莎教堂的這些窗戶在 12 月 1 日世界愛滋病日前裝好，正逢教堂成立一百週年。
窗上畫著不同年齡和背景的人。
教會說這提醒我們，愛滋病不會挑選它影響的對象。
其中一扇窗有愛滋紅絲帶、一段紀念逝者的文字，以及聖德蕾莎的紅玫瑰。
一道彩虹從一扇窗開始，延伸到另一扇窗。
第二扇窗有一朵獻給作家王爾德的綠色康乃馨，以及聖詹姆斯醫院的標誌，以感謝醫生和護理師。
底部的一排字母讓訪客能拼出他們失去的人的名字。
這些窗戶由教友和堂區團隊設計，並由一位教友出資。
當地公司 Capital Glass 負責製作和安裝。
堂區說這些窗戶是為所有人而設的，大家可以用自己的方式去理解。
這間教堂先前已有兩扇紀念新冠疫情期間死者的窗戶。

paragraphs: A Dublin church has installed two stained-glass windows in memory of people who died from Aids. The windows at St Teresa's Church on Donore Avenue were put in place ahead of World Aids Day on 1 December, during the church's centenary year.

Both windows depict people of various ages and cultural backgrounds, a reminder that the disease does not discriminate. The first features a red Aids ribbon, the red rose of St Teresa and an image of the Holy Spirit.

A rainbow stretches across both windows. The second includes a green carnation honouring Oscar Wilde, the logo of St James's Hospital as a tribute to medical staff, and ivy representing how widely the disease spread. An alphabet along the bottom allows visitors to spell out the name of a loved one.
The design was created by parishioners and members of the parish team, funded by a parishioner, and made by Capital Glass on Clanbrassil Street.

The parish described the installation as a huge honour and said visitors are free to interpret the windows in their own way. The church previously installed two windows commemorating those who died in the Covid pandemic.
sentZh: 都柏林一間教堂裝設了兩扇彩繪玻璃窗，紀念死於愛滋病的人。
多諾爾大道聖德蕾莎教堂的這些窗戶在 12 月 1 日世界愛滋病日前就位，時值教堂百年紀念。
兩扇窗都描繪了不同年齡和文化背景的人，提醒世人這種疾病不分對象。
第一扇窗的特色是愛滋紅絲帶、聖德蕾莎的紅玫瑰以及聖靈的圖像。
一道彩虹橫跨兩扇窗。
第二扇窗包含一朵向王爾德致敬的綠色康乃馨、向醫護人員致意的聖詹姆斯醫院標誌，以及象徵疾病傳播之廣的常春藤。
沿著底部的一排字母讓訪客能拼出所愛之人的名字。
這個設計由教友和堂區團隊成員構思，由一位教友出資，並由克蘭布拉西爾街的 Capital Glass 製作。
堂區形容能裝設這些窗戶是莫大的榮幸，並說訪客可以自由地以自己的方式詮釋它們。
這間教堂先前曾裝設兩扇窗，紀念在新冠疫情中去世的人。

paragraphs: A Dublin church has unveiled a pair of stained-glass windows commemorating those who lost their lives to Aids. Fitted at St Teresa's Church on Donore Avenue in the run-up to World Aids Day on 1 December, they coincide with the church's centenary.

Both panels portray people of diverse ages and cultural backgrounds, a poignant reminder that the illness is indiscriminate. The first bears a red Aids ribbon alongside the red rose of St Teresa and an emblem of the Holy Spirit.

A rainbow arcs from one window into the next. The second incorporates a green carnation paying homage to Oscar Wilde, the insignia of St James's Hospital in tribute to clinicians, and trailing ivy evoking the disease's relentless spread. An alphabet running along the base invites mourners to spell out the name of someone they have lost.
Conceived by parishioners and the parish team, the windows were financed by a benefactor from the congregation and crafted by Capital Glass on Clanbrassil Street.
The parish deemed it a tremendous honour to host them, stressing that visitors may interpret the imagery as they see fit. The church had already installed two windows in remembrance of Covid victims.
sentZh: 都柏林一間教堂揭幕了一對彩繪玻璃窗，悼念因愛滋病而失去生命的人。
這對窗戶在 12 月 1 日世界愛滋病日前夕裝設於多諾爾大道的聖德蕾莎教堂，恰逢教堂百年紀念。
兩片窗板都描繪了不同年齡與文化背景的人，令人心酸地提醒世人這種疾病不分對象。
第一扇窗上有愛滋紅絲帶，旁邊是聖德蕾莎的紅玫瑰和聖靈的象徵圖案。
一道彩虹從一扇窗以弧形延伸到另一扇窗。
第二扇窗融入了向王爾德致敬的綠色康乃馨、向臨床醫護人員致意的聖詹姆斯醫院徽記，以及令人聯想到疾病無情蔓延的垂掛常春藤。
沿著底部排列的字母讓哀悼者能拼出他們失去的人的名字。
這些窗戶由教友與堂區團隊構思，由會眾中的一位捐助者出資，並由克蘭布拉西爾街的 Capital Glass 精心製作。
堂區認為能安放這些窗戶是莫大的榮耀，並強調訪客可以按自己認為合適的方式詮釋其中的意象。
這間教堂先前已裝設兩扇窗，紀念新冠疫情的罹難者。

paragraphs: A church in Dublin has installed two stained-glass windows in commemoration of individuals who died as a result of Aids. The windows at St Teresa's Church on Donore Avenue were installed prior to World Aids Day on 1 December, coinciding with the centenary of the church.

Both windows depict individuals of diverse ages and cultural backgrounds, thereby emphasising that the disease does not discriminate. The first window incorporates a red Aids ribbon, the red rose of St Teresa and a representation of the Holy Spirit.

Furthermore, a rainbow extends across both windows. The second window contains a green carnation in honour of Oscar Wilde, the logo of St James's Hospital as an acknowledgement of healthcare professionals, and ivy symbolising the extensive spread of the disease. In addition, an alphabet along the base enables visitors to spell out the name of a deceased loved one.
The windows were designed collaboratively by parishioners and the parish team, financed by a parishioner and manufactured by Capital Glass on Clanbrassil Street.

The parish characterised the installation as a considerable honour and emphasised that visitors are free to interpret the windows as they consider appropriate. The church had previously installed two windows commemorating victims of the Covid pandemic.
